svg.title: bulkhead scan replaying Claude Code transcripts
svg.desc: An animated terminal. The command bulkhead scan is typed, then its real output appears: 14 transcripts, 527 shell commands, up to 4 sessions running at once, a table of 13 guard rules with hit counts counting up (checkout-guard stage-all 5, kill-guard pkill 5, disk-guard disk-wide-scan 3 and more), example commands such as git add -A, pkill node and du -sh ~, and the closing line: 24 commands in 13 sessions would have been stopped by bulkhead, 10 of them already stopped by a hook or declined.

g.text: bulkhead scan replaying your Claude Code sessions against the guards
read 14 transcripts (338 KB), 14 sessions, 527 shell commands in 0.1s
overlap up to 4 sessions running at once (Oct 29), 4 days with two or more at once
GUARD RULE HITS SESSIONS STOPPED LAST
checkout-guard stage-all 5 times in 5 sessions another session was active in the same tree at that minute
kill-guard pkill 5 times in 5 sessions kills by program name take down every session's servers
$ pkill node ~/code/acme-web Oct 29 [stopped by a hook]
disk-guard disk-wide-scan 3 times in 3 sessions whole-disk and parallel scans stall every session's I/O

A hit means the command had the shape a guard blocks, not that damage was done. port-guard and the low-RAM check
depend on what was running at that moment and are not replayed. checkout-guard is replayed from which sessions were
